key_insight: LLM coding agents can synthesize effective control policies directly from readable environment source code, reducing reliance on task-specific reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: For systems with accessible environment code, direct policy synthesis could reduce interaction costs while producing interpretable, executable decision rules.
method: Read environment source code to understand dynamics and constraints.
Translate this knowledge into executable control policies.
Refine policies using online feedback or offline data, without task-specific RL training.
evidence_signal: Across diverse decision-making benchmarks, synthesized policies matched or outperformed conventional RL methods with substantially less experience; comparisons also examined source-code access and challenging conditions.
watch_item: Applicability to systems without readable, faithful environment source code remains uncertain.
paper_title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
